models._note: Which Claude model backs each hte.roles function (bkt-hte-self-accounting). Values are CLI model aliases, passed straight through to `claude -p --model`. `escalation` is not a role; hte.roles.extract reaches for it when its three-member ensemble disagrees above the agreement threshold in hte/roles.py's EXTRACT_AGREEMENT_THRESHOLD.

meta_review.summary: Across the 271-hypothesis frontier, real evaluative differentiation is concentrated in a narrow slice of the label space (mostly 'maps-to'/entity-graph-resolver and 'parallels'/other-mechanism for the axial-age -1500..-571 window), while large swaths of the population are combinatorial padding: actor/place permutations around a few hub objects (confucius, deucalion, bahaullah, gilgamesh) that never receive distinct opinions. Opinion values repeat as exact floating-point duplicates across unrelated actor/object pairs, strongly suggesting the critic scores by action×mechanism template rather than per-hypothesis content, and several slots (exotic actions/mechanisms, skeptical/debunking readings, post-axial-age periods) are generated nominally but never actually explored with evidence.
flags: Templated/duplicated opinion floats (e.g. d=0.2518573002956571 appears on ~40+ 'parallels'+other-mechanism hypotheses; d=0.5594442696020775 on another ~15 unrelated actor/object pairs; d=0.6434580378246595 on all utnapishtim+parallels+other-mechanism cases) recur verbatim across unrelated content — evidence of scoring-by-bucket (action×mechanism) rather than per-hypothesis evaluation.

Action-slot stagnation: 'borrows-from', 'shares-etymology-with', 'structurally-echoes', 'precedes-chronologically', 'derives-from-common-source', 'common-source-reconstruction', 'other-action', and mechanism 'independent-invention'/'human-scholarly-comparison' are present in the label space but virtually every single instance sits at u=1.0 (b=0,d=0, i.e. completely unevaluated) — these relation types are being generated but never actually adjudicated anywhere in the 271-item population.

Mechanism-level belief bias: positive belief (b>0, ~17 hypotheses total) accrues almost exclusively to 'maps-to'+entity-graph-resolver claims in the -1500..-571/-1200..-1101 window; 'parallels'+other-mechanism hypotheses never once accrue belief, only fixed disbelief — the diffusion-vs-independent-parallel question looks pre-decided by mechanism label rather than by case-specific content.

'Confucius' hub artifact: dozens of hypotheses map unrelated actors (manu, abraham, david, krishna, rama, mahavira, zoroaster, guru-nanak, moses, muhammad, saoshyant, utnapishtim, joseph-smith, hyperdiffusionist-borrowing, euhemerist-deification) onto 'confucius' with place fixed to 'hinduism' regardless of Confucius's actual Chinese/Confucian context — looks like a place-field generation bug producing near-duplicate low-information hypotheses that inflate population count without adding distinct evidence.

Skeptical/debunking actor-hypotheses (mythicist-non-historicity, euhemerist-deification, channeled-modern-revelation) exist only as single, isolated instances with extremely low apriori weight 'a' (~0.018–0.047) and are frozen at u=1.0 — no genuinely dissenting/critical reading is ever explored or allowed to compete on comparable footing anywhere in the flood-myth/axial-age cluster.

Redundant place-only permutation clusters (manu×deucalion across hinduism/buddhism/greek/jainism/islam/lds/sikhism/judaism/other-place; david×gilgamesh across other-place/bahai/christianity/islam/judaism/jainism; buddha×bahaullah across buddhism/bahai/other-place/christianity) show identical or near-identical opinions regardless of place, indicating 'place' is varied combinatorially but not actually affecting evaluation — budget spent on non-informative permutations rather than genuine hypothesis diversity.

Temporal frontier gap: interval subdivision is fine-grained for -1500 to -500 (axial age) but the ~2300-year span from classical antiquity through medieval Islam/Christianity/LDS to the 19th-century Baha'i era collapses into one undifferentiated catch-all interval [-500,1863] used repeatedly for buddha/confucius/bahaullah/deucalion/jesus/laozi cross-era claims — no sub-periods (Hellenistic, Roman, Late Antique, Medieval, Early Modern) are ever tested separately in this later stretch.
recommended_actions: Recombine/deduplicate: collapse the place-only permutation clusters (manu-deucalion, david-gilgamesh, buddha-bahaullah, actor-confucius/hinduism) into single representative hypotheses per distinct mechanism, since opinions don't currently vary with place — free up population budget for genuinely new content.

Split off a dedicated sub-population to force real evidence-gathering on the currently-frozen exotic actions/mechanisms (borrows-from, shares-etymology-with, structurally-echoes, precedes-chronologically, derives-from-common-source, common-source-reconstruction, independent-invention, human-scholarly-comparison) instead of letting them default to u=1.0 indefinitely.

Widen: generate finer sub-period hypotheses across the -500..1863 gap (Hellenistic, Roman/Late Antique, Medieval Islamic/Christian/LDS-precursor, Early Modern) rather than reusing one giant undifferentiated catch-all interval for every cross-era Buddha/Confucius/Bahaullah claim.

Generalize/rebalance priors: raise apriori weight 'a' and actively solicit counter-evidence for skeptical/debunking actor-hypotheses (mythicist-non-historicity, euhemerist-deification, channeled-modern-revelation) so dissenting readings compete on equal footing rather than being permanently marginalized at near-zero prior.

Flag to pipeline engineering: audit whether opinion assignment is keyed off (action, mechanism) tuples rather than full hypothesis content — the exact repeated disbelief floats across unrelated actor/object pairs suggest a templated-scoring shortcut that should be corrected before the next generation round.

Fix/verify the place-field generation logic for 'confucius'-as-object hypotheses, which defaults to 'hinduism' regardless of the actor's or object's actual tradition, before letting this cluster expand further.
